item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 15, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Global advertising spending is expected to jump nearly 12 percent to $1.34 trillion this year, according to WARC Media. Social media leads the growth, with spending up more than 21 percent, while search and retail media also post double-digit gains. WARC expects the worldwide advertising market to reach $1.57 trillion by 2028, fueled by digital platforms and artificial intelligence.
In radio news,
iHeartMedia has revealed the lineup for its 2027 ALTer EGO concert, happening January 16th at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. The show features Evanescence, The Offspring, Billy Corgan, Death Cab for Cutie, Slightly Stoopid, Modest Mouse, Young the Giant, The Warning, and Temper City. Woody from ALT 98.7's nationally syndicated Woody Show will host. The concert will air live on iHeartRadio Alternative and Rock stations nationwide and through the iHeartRadio app. Tickets go on sale to the general public October 23rd, with earlier presales for eligible Capital One cardholders and ALT 98.7 VIP members.
Turning to digital media,
M-I-W is accepting applications for its third annual Digital Sales Mentorship Program. One woman working in radio or digital media sales will receive a year of personalized coaching, covering digital marketing, streaming, podcasting, revenue strategies and leadership development. Applicants must have at least three years of sales experience. The deadline is November sixth. Details are available at Radio M-I-W dot com.
In radio news,
Cumulus Media’s NewsTalk 580 and 105.9 K-M-J in Fresno has raised a record 428 thousand dollars for the Central California Food Bank. The station partnered with Gar Incorporated for its 13th annual Feeding Families Fund Drive. The one-day event will provide more than 1.7 million meals to families in need. Over 13 years, the campaign has raised more than 5.5 million dollars.
Turning to music,
Warner Records Group has named longtime music executive Jim Roppo Vice Chairman. Roppo joins after nearly three decades at Universal Music Group, most recently serving as Chairman and CEO of Republic Records. Based in Los Angeles, he'll oversee operations across Warner's labels and report to Chairman and CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck. His start date has not been announced.
On the business side of media,
Meta AI's Bridget Bogee says the future of artificial intelligence will move beyond chatbots toward personalized digital assistants that manage work and everyday responsibilities. Speaking during the Alliance for Women in Media's October Office Hours, Bogee emphasized that human creativity and judgment remain essential. Her career advice? “Go where you’re wanted,” encouraging professionals to seek leaders who recognize their talents.
And finally,
In Indianapolis, 99.5 ZPL's Smiley Morning Show is celebrating its 24th annual Pumpkin Drop Today at the Indiana State Fairgrounds. The free family event features a nearly fourteen-hundred-pound pumpkin crashing from hundreds of feet above the ground, plus trick-or-treating, games and entertainment. The big splat happens around eight Thursday morning.
Find more media news, jobs, industry resources and free tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
